go whoring verb

also visit prostitutes, whore around, go with prostitutes, frequent brothels, whore (verb)

classical

Ter. Ad. 102: scortārī neque pōtāre
Plaut. Asin. 270: quandō mēcum pariter pōtant, pariter scortārī solent

scortor, scortārī

verb, first conjugation, deponent

go with prostitutes, whore

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

From scortum. Varro defines it: scortārī est saepius meretrīculam dūcere (LL 7.84, Lewis & Short). Ante- and post-classical.

Examples

  • Nōn est flāgitium, mihi crēde, adulēscentulum scortārī neque pōtāre.

    It is no outrage, believe me, for a young man to go whoring or drinking.Ter. Ad. 101–102

  • nam sī istuc jūs est, senectā aetāte scortārī senēs, ubi locīst rēs summa nostra pūblica?

    for if that is the rule, that old men go whoring in their old age, where does that leave our commonwealth?Plaut. Merc. 985–986

See also prostitute, whoremonger, brothel, live it up.

SourcesLewis & Short: scortor

Plautus, Asinaria 270; Mercator 985–986. Terence, Adelphoe 101–102.
